source_locations: Cambridge article header and abstract, lines 437–500: title, author, online publication date, DOI, and abstract.
§3.1, lines 572–587: Poisson NNTuck generative model, nonnegative U/V/Y and core tensor G; fitting by maximum likelihood is equivalent to minimizing KL divergence.

checks.abstract: PASS; note reproduces the Cambridge abstract.

checks.research_questions: PASS; accurately condenses the motivating question and stated contribution.
checks.model: FAIL; model family and high-level variants are correctly identified, but the testing/fitting account is materially incomplete. The note says nested models are compared with likelihood-ratio tests without stating that ordinary Wilks LRT assumptions fail for this nonidentifiable model and that the paper instead uses split-LRT, with its own caveats and especially weak guarantees for SCA. It describes the SCA fit only as a heuristic update; source Algorithm 2 gives a defining initialization and ordered V→U→Y updates and warns the update is not monotone or guaranteed to converge. These are material parts of the proposed test/model procedure.

findings: Clarify exact inference method: define the split-LRT comparison and its caveats, including SCA-specific caution; do not imply standard LRT validity.
Expose the SCA update procedure and its limitations, or clearly label it as an approximate fitting procedure with the actual initialization and update order.
